backing.attachment_point_basis: $20.0M loss-waterfall junior layer over a $251,805,229 ALL-CHAIN senior (Re /tvl, 2026-09-06). Both operands same-dated. NOT the ~$73M balance-sheet figure -- DIFFERENT QUANTITIES: loss absorption follows what the treaties subordinate, and the 105-110% band on a $358M premium book is ~$17.9M. BASIS DISCIPLINE, CORRECTED 2026-09-06: the senior must be read ALL-CHAIN. The Ethereum leg alone is $235,644,130 today -- 93.6% of the all-chain total, down from 97.1% on 2026-08-11 as other chains grew -- so an Ethereum-only denominator OVERSTATES the attachment point by roughly 30-60bps and the gap widens over time. A prior version of this field claimed the published 9.66% (2026-08-24) 'reproduces exactly on this same basis'. IT DOES NOT: that figure divided by the ETHEREUM LEG ALONE ($207.0M), so it was a differently-derived number wearing the same label -- precisely what this field exists to catch, asserted backwards. On an all-chain basis 2026-08-24 was ~9.0-9.4%, already below the 9.66% published.
backing.attachment_point_direction_note: THINNED BECAUSE THE DENOMINATOR ROSE, not because the junior layer shrank. No loss occurred; senior deposits grew. A supply series alone reads as strength while the cushion erodes.
backing.eligible_sleeve_note: ⚠️ THIS IS A MANDATE, NOT A COMPOSITION. These are the assets the on-chain liquid sleeve is PERMITTED to hold. The MEASURED reserve is 98.97% sUSDe (see protocol_reserves_passthrough). T-Bills are an allowed rotation that HAS NOT OCCURRED. Reading the eligible set as the holding makes a single-asset book look diversified.

backing.attachment_point_vintage_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-06, AND IT RESOLVED ADVERSELY -- retained rather than deleted so the page does not silently lose that this figure was ever hedged. The prior note said INDICATIVE, NOT MEASURED: a June 2026 junior figure over an August on-chain senior read, ~2 months apart, and reasoned the true figure was 'more likely BELOW 9.66% than above it' because the denominator was the operand that grew. That reasoning REQUIRED the junior layer to be flat, which was an assumption. It is now a measurement: the residual junior proxy is +0.4% over three weeks against senior growth of +39.3%. The hedge was correct in direction and the figure moved the way it predicted.
backing.backing_score_basis: AUTHORED, NOT COMPUTED -- a FALLBACK that yields to any derived collateral ratio; PegTracker declares no ratio establishable for this asset (Re publishes combined reUSD + reUSDe reserves with no asset-attributed denominator). CUT 5.5 -> 5.0 on 2026-09-06. The 5.5 rested on two reasons and the FIRST moved: it cited an attachment point of 9.66% as already below the 10% norm, and it is 7.94% today -- 21% thinner in 13 days, the fourth consecutive reading in the same direction, and now basis-independent. NOTHING IN THE REINSURANCE BOOK DETERIORATED: no claim event, combined ratio still 92%, no treaty ever above 99%, collateral quality unchanged. This is dilution by growth. The reserve is also 99.05% sUSDe as measured -- 'USDC, USDe, sUSDe, T-Bills' is the sleeve's ELIGIBLE SET, not its composition, and the T-Bill rotation has not occurred; that concentration is priced on axis 4 (dependencies 5.0), not here, so it is stated but not double-counted. Not lower than 5.0: the second reason behind the original 5.5 (issuer-written NAV on SharePriceCalculator) is unchanged, and the loss threshold still requires a ~115% combined ratio against a realised 92%.
backing.backing_score_applies_when_note: ⚠️ MUST NOT fire on a merely-absent collateral_ratio. The producer declares this one underivable in collateral_ratio_basis. A bare null can also mean a failed fetch or a feed outage — and promoting an authored score over a measurement that exists but did not load is the failure where a failed read lands wherever the substitute sits. Require the DECLARATION, not the absence.
backing.attachment_point_basis_independent_note: The decline holds on BOTH of Re's contradictory junior figures: 11.06% -> 7.94% on the $20M waterfall basis, and 40.36% -> 28.98% on the ~$73M balance-sheet basis. Every earlier instance of this finding was arguable on the grounds that the $77M-vs-$20M question was unresolved. This one is not, which is why it moved a score when three prior readings did not.
backing.junior_capital_basis: Residual non-tokenized capital, computed from Re /tvl as onchain_capital ($165,400,740) + offchain_capital ($179,524,465) - (reUSD $251,805,229 + reUSDe $20,152,024) = $72,967,952. This is the BALANCE-SHEET junior (~$73M / the '$77M' product-page figure), NOT the $20.0M waterfall layer the attachment ratio divides by -- the two are different quantities and must not be substituted for one another. Published so the tile is self-verifying: it is the numerator's sibling, measured from the same payload, and it is what establishes that the junior layer is FLAT (~$72.7M on 2026-08-13, +0.4%).
backing.attachment_point_series_note: CLEAN ALL-CHAIN SERIES, one basis throughout: 2026-08-11 $180.8M -> 11.06% | 2026-09-04 $243.6M -> 8.21% | 2026-09-06 $251.8M -> 7.94%. Senior growth +39.3% over that window is UNAFFECTED by the basis error, because both endpoints are /tvl all-chain. The 2026-08-24 reading is deliberately EXCLUDED from the series: its $207.0M was an Ethereum-leg measurement and is not comparable to the points either side of it. Caught by tidresearch, who declined to publish a trend line whose denominator might change definition between points, and were right to. The direction and the score are unchanged -- on a clean basis the decline is 11.06% -> 7.94%, LARGER than the mixed series implied, not smaller.
